findings.quote: two of the JS ten share a class — the :47-48 pair
findings.why: The parenthetical undercounts shared-class defects in the cited Kimi manifest. Its table has D1 `off-by-one count` and D2 `off-by-one count (findings cap)` at :44-45, plus D4/D5 `dropped arm` at :47-48. The bash example is consistent with its tally (`dropped branch 1/2` at Kagi :78-80).

notes: Step 5 names a `--check` uniqueness gate and requires literal `all unique`, but the historical `mutate_driver.py` is absent from this tree and the maintained `tools/mutate-and-run.sh` rejects `--check` (exit 64). Its APPLY output differs; Restore discipline item 6 discloses the historical driver is one-off/not in-tree, but this section does not provide a runnable substitute for a new sweep.

The next section says `One defect per class per sweep` (SKILL.md:276-278), whereas this section says `at least one per class` and points to examples with repeated classes; clarify which governs new sweeps.
The JS shared-class parenthetical omits D1/D2 at Kimi :44-45; the note's own by-class tally at :55-57 shows `off-by-one 1/2` as well as `dropped arm 2/2`.
The model citation names Kimi §1 and §3-§6 but omits §2 (surviving-defect analysis), although step 8 cites Kimi :82-99 from §2.

This section uses the current `$HYAKU_SCRATCH/<lane>-r<round>/<sub>/` shape, while the historical Kill-rate bands section and appendices retain `/tmp/<lane>-r<round>-<n>-work/`; the former matches Standing rules, the latter is historical wording.
The recipe does not designate a concrete target artifact in step 1; round-16 CR04a reported this as a minor gap, resolving it by choosing the cited Kimi model artifact.

The maintained driver adjudicates KILLED on nonzero exit alone, while step 7 requires verdict/count adjudication. In a scratch fixture, the mutant printed `SELFTEST: FAIL (1 cases)` but exited 0; the driver recorded SURVIVED. The section names the maintained driver for other behaviors but does not state which verdict rule governs.
